text:
maya: Heads-up — CI perf smoke on release-2026-03: p99 for small-chat-v1 jumped ~25% after the merge. This is a rollout blocker for the hosted pool. benchmark-bot attached numbers. Can someone run a git bisect and try to repro locally? :warning:

benchmark-bot: nightly-perf job 1768000109 — status: FAILED. baseline p99=168ms -> current p99=210ms. tokens/sec -18%. Full artifact: https://ci.redwood/1768000109/logs

liam: I'm on it, starting git bisect on my devbox. Repro note: use single GPU, --seq-len 512 --batch 8, 100 iters, warmup 20.

sasha: Quick update from my local bisect: I hit the bad range quickly. Suspect the kernel-selector + batching-heuristic refactor (PR #2142 / commit c4f2a7d).

sasha: git bisect snippet:
```
$ git bisect start f9e8d7a bad a1b2c3f good
bisecting: 10 revisions left to test after this (roughly)
# commit c4f2a7d: Adjust kernel selection heuristics and default tokens-per-batch
 tested: run_perf --model small-chat-v1 --seq 512 --batch 8
Result: p99=212ms (bad)
# commit b3d9e12: minor logging
Result: p99=171ms (good)
```

liam: I reproduced the regression and narrowed it to the same commit (c4f2a7d). Profiling summary (nvprof / tinyprof) below.

liam: profiler aggregates (weighted):
```
Before (a1b2c3): flash_attn kernels: 60% time, fused_kv: 5%, memcpy: 10%, runtime_overhead: 2%
After (c4f2a7d): flash_attn: 42%, fallback_matmul_fp32: 28%, memcpy: 18%, runtime_overhead: 6%
```

liam: Observations: the selector now prefers smaller token batches which increases kernel-switch frequency and triggers suboptimal matmul path for certain heads. Net effect: more memcpy + kernel launch overhead on 64k token workloads.

sasha: The batching change in the refactor lowered the default target_tokens_per_batch from 4096 -> 2048 for medium models. That explains why for seq=512/batch=8 we fall into a different kernel regime.

maya: Good catch. Options: (A) revert commit c4f2a7d, (B) tweak runtime config to restore old default for tokens-per-batch, or (C) add explicit kernel preference map per model. Which is least risky?

ops: Hold the rollout to 10% until we have a mitigation. I've paused the canary in the console.

dev-bot: deploy-checker: canary paused by ops at 1768000300 — reason: perf regression p99 +25%

liam: I'm preparing a small patch that restores tokens-per-batch default and adds a guard: skip the new selector when seq_len >= 512 and model_type == "decoder-transformer". Patch branch: fix/batch-default-restore.

sasha: Quick reproducible command for others:
```
# checkout the bad commit to confirm
git checkout c4f2a7d
./scripts/run_perf.sh --model small-chat-v1 --seq 512 --batch 8 --warmup 20 --iters 100
# then checkout the good commit
git checkout a1b2c3
./scripts/run_perf.sh --model small-chat-v1 --seq 512 --batch 8 --warmup 20 --iters 100
```

maya: If patch looks good, can we do a hotfix revert to unblock rollout and follow up with a proper kernel-selector fix?

liam: Patch runs locally: p99 restored to ~169ms on my 3090 devbox. I'll open the PR with bench logs + bisect evidence. ETA ~30m.

sasha: I'll run the CI perf job against fix/batch-default-restore once the PR is up.

ops: Thanks — keep me posted. If CI confirms, I'll unpause canary and bump to 50% in stages.

maya: Sweet. Assigning follow-ups: @liam PR + bench artifacts; @sasha CI verification; @ops hold/unhold rollout. ping me if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
